clue.text: Getting characters to conform to order

definitions.text: Getting characters to conform to order

parts.words: Getting characters to conform to order
parts.note: characters read as letters of the alphabet, and the order is A to Z, so this describes sorting words letter by letter

explanation.definitionFit: Putting words into A-to-Z sequence by their letters is exactly the process of sorting by the alphabet.

clue.text: Accepting a sin — smug, sloppy

indicators.note: something sloppy is careless and disordered, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone tolerates a wrongdoing with a self-satisfied, careless air.
explanation.definitionFit: Presuming or taking on, as in assuming responsibility, is a synonym of accepting.

clue.text: Man loudly exchanging letters shows no gentle persuasion

indicators.note: two letters in the phrase swap places: the C of the man's name trades with the T of the musical term

parts.note: Bruce is a man's name
forte is the musical direction for playing loudly

explanation.surface: A man raising his voice and trading insults is clearly not using gentle persuasion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exchanging letters' swaps the C and T in BRUCE FORTE, giving BRUTE FORCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheer strength used instead of tact is the opposite of gentle persuasion; the definition describes what such an approach amounts to.

clue.text: Courses — they have 21 for the riders who are running

definitions.meaning: the first dishes of a meal, the soup or appetiser before the main

definitions.text: they have 21 for the riders who are running
definitions.meaning: officials who begin a horse race give instructions (21 = orders) to the jockeys taking part

explanation.definitionFit: First-course dishes are called this, and so are the race officials who send the field on its way.

clue.text: Where there's a will with no introduction, it's complex

indicators.note: the first letter of the word is dropped, as if it lost its introduction

parts.note: testate describes a person who died having made a valid will

explanation.surface: A proverb about willpower is twisted into a remark that things are complicated.
explanation.walkthrough: The proverb 'where there's a will, there's a way' is a decoy; here it means the legal state of having left a will. 'with no introduction' removes its first T.
explanation.definitionFit: A housing complex is a group of buildings, as in a council or industrial development of that kind.

clue.text: Not knowing accompaniment to 3 23?

definitions.meaning: a state of lacking knowledge or awareness
the stock phrase pairs crude strength (3 23) with a lack of understanding: 'brute force and ...'

explanation.definitionFit: Lack of knowledge is the plain sense, and the idiom 'brute force and ignorance' supplies the companion.

clue.text: Hello, there's fog about! It can get one caught out

definitions.text: It can get one caught out

indicators.note: the fog word goes round the greeting, sitting about it

parts.note: mist is a light fog
hi is an informal hello

explanation.surface: Someone greets a friend while commenting on foggy weather.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a batter who is 'caught out' is dismissed when a fielder catches the ball, often off a badly struck shot.
explanation.definitionFit: A poorly struck ball in cricket can loop up to a fielder, so the batter is caught.

clue.text: A fry the steak bar cooked?

definitions.text: A fry the steak bar cooked?

indicators.note: cooked means prepared or doctored, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether a grill bar prepared a fry-up.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the anagram and a description of a big fried morning meal served by a steak bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A substantial fried morning meal, the full English, is exactly a fry such a bar might cook.

clue.text: Pre-death observance played out — girl comes round!

indicators.note: the girl word encloses the other piece, coming round it

parts.note: lass is a girl, especially in Scotland and northern England
trite means overused, stale, played out

explanation.surface: A death-bed scene in which a girl regains consciousness just as the ritual ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes round' suggests reviving, but it is the container indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: The sacraments given to a dying person are a religious observance before death.

clue.text: Person in uniform teased within earshot

indicators.note: what can be heard rather than read, so the word is taken by its sound

parts.note: to guy someone is to ridicule or tease them

explanation.surface: Someone in uniform was mocked where they could hear it.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'guy' is an old verb for poking fun at someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of the Girl Guides wears a uniform, so she is a person in uniform.

clue.text: The woman's relation entering as ghost, maybe

indicators.note: the relation word goes into the possessive pronoun

parts.note: her is the possessive for a woman
an aunt is a relation

explanation.surface: A woman's relative is pictured as a ghost.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that frequents a place spectrally, as a ghost does, is one example of such a visitor.

clue.text: A second source of pollen containing nothing

indicators.note: the flower part holds the zero letter inside it

parts.note: an anther is the part of a stamen that produces pollen
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A botanical remark about a second flower part that has nothing in it.
explanation.definitionFit: One more, a further one, is what 'a second' means in 'have a second helping'.

clue.text: Taunt one coming in to face bowling

indicators.note: the numeral letter enters the cricket word

parts.note: in cricket the batter bats to face the bowling
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: Jeering at a cricketer walking in to bat.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket: to bat is to face the bowler's deliveries.
explanation.definitionFit: To bait someone is to tease or provoke them, a synonym of taunt.

clue.text: Try to avoid paying debts? Bank comes round in the proper manner

indicators.note: the bank word encloses the debt-dodging verb

parts.note: to bank on is to rely on
to levant is to abscond leaving debts unpaid, especially gambling debts

explanation.surface: A debtor dodges payment and the bank comes chasing.
explanation.walkthrough: LEVANT is a rare British verb for running off without paying what is owed; 'Bank' is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: Pertinently, in a fitting way, is an adverb close to 'in the proper manner'.

clue.text: Once again serve raw meat injected with drug

indicators.note: the drug letter is put inside the meat pieces

parts.note: red means raw, as with rare meat
liver is offal eaten as meat
E is ecstasy, the drug

explanation.surface: Raw meat laced with a drug is served up again.
explanation.definitionFit: To serve again, as with a summons or a parcel, is to hand it over once more.

clue.text: Ferocious female, one with good lot of hair around

indicators.note: the hair word wraps round the two other letters

parts.note: a tress is a lock of hair
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A fierce woman with a mane of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A female big cat is proverbially fierce, and the word also describes a fierce woman.

clue.text: A creep's tricky — one may be seen getting away!

definitions.text: one may be seen getting away

indicators.note: tricky means awkward or slippery, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A sneaky fellow is spotted making off.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is' here, so its S is part of the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who runs off from prison or captivity is a fugitive, a person getting away.

clue.text: Part of New York is sedate after turmoil

indicators.note: turmoil is confusion, so the letters have been thrown about

explanation.surface: A calm place becomes so only after chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: The East Side is a district of Manhattan, so it is a named area of the city.

clue.text: Code of behaviour set down by first army officer?

parts.note: proto- is a prefix meaning first
Col is the abbreviation for colonel

explanation.surface: Etiquette laid down by the senior officer.
explanation.definitionFit: Official rules of etiquette and procedure form a formal code of conduct.

clue.text: Big nag should be quiet! — anger shown by husband, awfully sore

parts.note: sh is the call for silence
ire is anger

indicators.note: awfully suggests badly done, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A scold is told to hush while an angry husband is sore.
explanation.walkthrough: 'nag' looks like a scold but means a horse.
explanation.definitionFit: A heavy English draught horse is a large horse, and nag is a slang word for a horse.

clue.text: I would fish, sitting by the river maybe?

parts.note: I'd is the contraction of I would
ling is a long cod-like fish

explanation.surface: Someone says they would go fishing, perhaps sitting on the riverbank.
explanation.definitionFit: Lazing about doing nothing, as one might on a riverbank, is an example of loafing.

clue.text: Does Right Reverend get involved in monastic communities?

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: taken as written
RR is the abbreviation for Right Reverend, a bishop's title

explanation.surface: A question whether a bishop joins in with monks.
explanation.definitionFit: Religious orders such as the Benedictines are communities of monks or nuns.

clue.text: Thermal insulation rating attached to a garment

parts.note: tog is a unit measuring warmth of duvets and clothing

explanation.surface: The warmth rating label is sewn onto an item of clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: The loose robe of ancient Rome is a classic garment.

clue.text: See 3
Agreed an end to engagement, getting married

indicators.note: the final letter of the word is taken

parts.note: allied means joined or united, as in marriage

explanation.surface: A couple's engagement ends with a wedding.
explanation.definitionFit: Figures that tally correspond, so the verb means matched or agreed.

clue.text: Vain type, who so surprisingly attracts more than one female

indicators.note: surprisingly hints at an unexpected order, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: F is female, doubled to FF for the plural

explanation.surface: A vain man who, unexpectedly, draws several women.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who flaunts themselves is a vain exhibitionist type.

clue.text: No longer unit to be included?

definitions.text: No longer unit to be included?

indicators.note: the unit letter is put inside the other word

parts.note: once means formerly, no longer so
U is short for unit

explanation.surface: A question whether an obsolete measure should still be counted.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue describes the measure: an imperial unit no longer in official use.
explanation.definitionFit: This small imperial weight has been replaced by grams, so it is a unit no longer used.

clue.text: Left-wing performers who may mess around with the text?

definitions.text: who may mess around with the text?

parts.note: red means left-wing, socialist
actors are performers

explanation.surface: Socialist actors who tamper with the script.
explanation.definitionFit: Editors prepare or censor text, which can mean messing about with it.
